qualification: local development evidence; not signed release qualification

hotPathRanking.owner: flat guest-physical reservation plus inline software TLB
hotPathRanking.interpretation: Translation and Swift memory-helper boundaries are nearly per-instruction, while actual page walks are rare. Remove the boundary and inline the hit path before optimizing the walker.
Per-block generation proof is paid roughly once every 2.8 instructions, but almost never invalidates. Replace repeated checks with protected-page invalidation after the flat memory base exists.

hotPathRanking.owner: direct block chaining and indirect-branch prediction
hotPathRanking.interpretation: Natural blocks are short and only 1.46% of completed blocks use the existing chained path. Direct chaining follows D02-D04 because it should consume the new inline memory/TLB and invalidation contracts.

hotPathRanking.owner: pinned guest registers and lazy flags
hotPathRanking.interpretation: Register and flag materialization are not independently timed by the current counters. The high block-boundary incidence makes D06 plausible, but its benefit must be isolated after D05 rather than assigned a fabricated wall share.

pageWalker.reason: Only 0.1886% of translation requests walked page tables; optimizing the rare walker before the hit path is not supported.

deviceMMIO.reason: MMIO is measured but too infrequent to lead the CPU redesign.

timerRequests.reason: Timer requests are measured but too infrequent to lead the CPU redesign.

singleVCPU64InstructionCap.reason: The measured one-vCPU path uses a bounded 4096-instruction fairness limit; the 64-instruction limit remains only while multiple processors are runnable.

orderedWork: A04.2 inline TLB and flat-address fast path
A05.1 register convention and lazy flags
A05.2 direct chaining, IBTC, and shadow return stack
decision.reason: The measurement confirms that memory translation/helper boundaries dominate hot-path incidence, followed by generation checks and block dispatch.

limitations: Hot-path percentages are event incidence rates per retired instruction, not sub-phase wall-time shares.
The counters select architecture order but do not claim the unimplemented changes meet G1-G5.
The source run was a local release build with opt-in instrumentation, not a signed or notarized candidate.
